ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • Barney and Betty Hill, an interracial American couple from Portsmouth, New Hampshire, claimed they were abducted by extraterrestrials in the White Mountains on the night of September 19-20, 1961 - the first widely publicized claim of alien abduction.
  • The Hills reported roughly two hours of missing time after seeing a bright light and a craft while driving home from Montreal; Betty's dress was stained and torn, Barney's shoes badly scuffed.
  • Their story was adapted into the best-selling 1966 book 'The Interrupted Journey' by John Fuller and NBC's 1975 TV film 'The UFO Incident'.
  • In July 2011 the New Hampshire Division of Historical Resources placed a historical marker at the site of the alleged craft's first approach; Betty Hill's notes and tapes are archived at the University of New Hampshire.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Betty Hill (1961) — Social worker; claimed she was taken aboard a craft and shown a star map later associated with the Zeta Reticuli system.
  • Barney Hill (1961) — Postal worker; claimed through binoculars to have seen non-human figures in a cigar-shaped craft hovering over their car.
